item.title: River's Rocket Works
item.description: A rocket game I built for River. Design a rocket, fly twelve missions from first launch to a wormhole, and race the whole family around the solar system.

item.title: Putting our buses on the map, live
item.description: How I turned the GPS units already on our buses into a GTFS Realtime feed, and a live map for the public.

item.title: Making a Sunfish faster without breaking the rules
item.description: My tuning notes for the Sunfish: the four sail controls, a few ideas I want to test, and the only class-legal way to rig a vang.

item.title: A driving game set on our real bus routes
item.description: A 3D driving game in the browser built from real route data, real streets and about 40,000 real building footprints. It started as a trolley simulator and kept growing.

item.title: A sailing simulator you steer with your hands
item.description: A browser sailing game that watches your hands through the webcam. Pick a Sunfish, an Optimist or a pirate ship.

item.title: A dispatch board for when a driver calls in
item.description: An eight-week driver rotation in a spreadsheet, plus a one-page board that works out who covers which route when someone calls in.

item.title: Replacing the paratransit spreadsheets
item.description: A small web app for booking paratransit rides, assigning drivers and producing the reports, built with Node.js, Express and SQLite.

item.title: A countdown sign for bus stops, built from a $32 board
item.description: Commercial e-paper bus stop signs cost thousands of dollars each. I'm building a single-stop prototype around a $32 e-paper board and a long-range radio.

item.title: A wizard that fills out the procurement forms
item.description: A single-page tool that asks plain questions about a purchase and produces the right determination form, with the checks that are easy to forget.

item.title: Color a bus, then watch it save the day
item.description: A printable coloring page and a small story app that puts a kid's own hand-colored bus into an adventure, ending with a certificate.

item.title: A free week of sailing lessons every June
item.description: I'm the commodore of our local yacht club, and every June we teach people to sail for free. Here's what the week is and why we do it.

item.title: How to score a race when the boats don't match
item.description: Club races put fast boats and slow boats on the same course. The Portsmouth yardstick is the simple math that makes it fair.

item.title: F1 wings for a two-seat go-kart
item.description: River loves Formula 1, so the Thunder Kart I'm rebuilding is getting a front wing, a rear wing and sidepods. Plywood, PVC pipe and about $50.

item.title: Formula 1 keeps showing up in everything I build
item.description: A kart racer, a go-kart with wings and a Grand Prix hidden inside a bus simulator. A short tour of how one kid's favorite sport took over my projects.

item.title: Comics and picture books starring River
item.description: Two picture books about our family and a three-part space comic that sneaks in relativity and quantum mechanics.

item.title: How this site got built
item.description: A domain, a free host, no framework and four rounds of me saying "I don't like it yet." Notes on building r3ai.dev with Claude.

item.title: 27 ways I actually use AI
item.description: A list of every kind of thing I have used AI for, at work and at home, with a short post on each. Start here.

item.title: Getting a straight answer on a regulation
item.description: Four small federal funding and accessibility questions that can each eat an afternoon, and how I ask them now.

item.title: A sanity check before you call the attorney
item.description: A church invited us to bring a bus to a community event. I used AI to understand the question before I took it to legal.

item.title: Turning what you see in the field into a business case
item.description: We keep meeting riders we cannot talk to. Here is how a real problem at the bus door became a funding memo Finance could approve.

item.title: Asking AI what a document is missing
item.description: I had a morning meeting about an old scope of work for a backup generator. I asked one question: what is wrong with this, and what is not in it?

item.title: Everyday email: tone, humor and the question you forgot to answer
item.description: I asked AI to make two emails funnier. It did, and it also noticed that one of them never answered the question I was asked.

item.title: Writing a careful public reply
item.description: When a resident asks whether a rumor is true, the wording matters. Here is how I draft those replies, including the time the AI got ahead of the facts.

item.title: Checklists, flyers and forms in an afternoon
item.description: Cleaning checklists, a fare flyer, a staff reference sheet, a fillable form and an anonymous suggestion box. None of it is glamorous. All of it used to wait.

item.title: Building a procedure library and closing audit findings
item.description: A federal review left us with findings and a deadline. Here is how AI helped turn scattered old documents into procedures we can actually follow.

item.title: Untangling grant money before a deadline
item.description: Several older grants, a handful of invoices and a date after which the money goes away. AI did the matching and found the invoices that did not fit.

item.title: Turning a policy into a tool
item.description: I wanted to save our purchasing staff some work on small purchases. That turned into a memo, then a form, then a wizard that writes the paperwork.

item.title: A consultant-grade plan from documents already on hand
item.description: A consultant asked for our transit plan. We did not have a stand-alone one. Here is how the documents we did have became a 14-page plan.

item.title: Building the case for a new service, then rebuilding it
item.description: I spent weeks on a presentation about on-demand transit. Then one of my assumptions turned out to be wrong, and the whole thing had to be rebuilt as something else.

item.title: Preparing for a hard meeting in an hour
item.description: I had a disagreement over how a written policy should be read, and a meeting in sixty minutes. I asked AI to argue the other side.

item.title: Checking the numbers before you reply
item.description: Someone sent me a total. Before I agreed or disagreed, I had AI read the rulebook and recount.

item.title: Building custom software without being a professional developer
item.description: I taught myself to build web pages. With AI doing a large share of the typing, I now build the tools my division needs when nothing off the shelf fits.

item.title: Organizing the work itself
item.description: Before my assistant manager and I sat down to sort out everything on our plates, I asked AI how to run that meeting.

item.title: Community partnerships and a coloring app
item.description: Transit is a public service, and the public should like it. Two small examples of using AI for the community side of the job.

item.title: When the AI is wrong, and when it says no
item.description: The most useful post in this series. The mistakes I caught, the ones I nearly did not, and the requests the AI turned down.

item.title: Building games for my kid
item.description: I am not a game developer. Here is how one request became a twelve-mission space game with our whole family in it, and what I learned about directing an AI.

item.title: A hometown bus simulator from real map data
item.description: It started as a toy trolley on a made-up grid. It became a driving game on our real streets, with real routes and tens of thousands of real buildings.

item.title: A father-son comic book about physics
item.description: River wrote a space adventure about the biggest unsolved problem in physics. We are turning it into a real printed comic book.

item.title: Standing up a website in a weekend
item.description: This site is brand new. Here is what I did, what the AI did, and why I could not load my own website the day it went live.

item.title: Pure fun: a goat racer trailer and texts to my dad
item.description: Not everything has to be useful. A 30-second movie trailer made from one photo, and a running joke about my dad's car.

item.title: Small life questions
item.description: A benefits document, a scraped bumper and a strange name on a restaurant. Three everyday questions and what I learned from asking them.

item.title: Hobbies and volunteering: sailing scores and a club website
item.description: I race small sailboats and help run a yacht club. AI now does the race arithmetic and some of the homework a volunteer board never has time for.

item.title: Chasing a big idea, and letting AI poke holes in it
item.description: I have a concept for helping local governments modernize. The most valuable thing AI did was make my own numbers smaller.

item.title: Following curiosity into hard math
item.description: I am not a mathematician. I spent many hours with an AI on one of the most famous unsolved problems anyway.

item.title: Sloth Rocket Grand Prix: a kart racer in one HTML file
item.description: I asked an AI for a kart racer themed on Formula 1, rockets, pirates, libraries and sloths. Here is what came back, how to play it and where it falls short.

item.title: What goes in the work section
item.description: A short note on what I plan to write about from the transit side, and what I'll leave out.
